geometry_edits.rationale: Align the public threshold cut to the verified access side.
Increase the apparent width of the access carve for a clearer entry seam.
Keep the carved threshold low and usable at ground.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the public threshold on the verified access side while preserving the dominant stepped mass.
Widen the entry carve so it reads as an actual usable public cut rather than a minor clip.
Keep the notch grounded and useful at the street edge without breaking the primary massing gesture.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one dominant stepped mass with clear hierarchy, so it is not rejected for fragmentation or view mismatch. The parcel response is acceptable: the orange mass sits within the green boundary and the long axis turns in a way that feels related to the site, rather than merely filling the box. The main weakness is that the verified access edge is answered only weakly; there is some ground relief and a small lower-volume seam, but no strongly legible public court or entry carve aligned to the frontage. The silhouette is coherent and capacity-bearing rather than arbitrary, and the section has a plausible terraced logic for neighborhood living. Overall it is program-appropriate for compact mixed neighborhood living, but it would be stronger with a cleaner, more explicit carved public threshold at the access edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and curved; candidate is tighter and more rectilinear.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise massing with a central void and an upper connector can create a readable civic/community threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Sports mall typology and circular ring plan are not directly transferable to this compact block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A perimeter mass organized around an open center can support neighborhood/public use while keeping the ground legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Aerial campus composition is too dispersed and tower-based compared with the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, campus-like aggregation can preserve hierarchy while opening a public courtyard/plaza.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is flatter and more open at ground than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A large carved void and overhanging upper mass can produce an active civic threshold from a simple prism.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more horizontally spread and site-responsive than the candidate’s compact stepped block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise mass with a courtyard void and folded/terraced roof reads as neighborhood-serving and public.

warnings: Access-edge response is present but under-articulated; the ground condition could be more public and legible.
